findings.title: The pull request says the pre-registrations were committed before any fix code and before any test run. Its own second pre-registration records prototypes and test runs made before it was committed, and the receipt gate's 386 cases and the new wiring cases were never pre-registered at all.

findings.expected: The status line says what happened. The first pre-registration (7df03f2) came before every change. The second (48c7bfc) was committed after two prototypes and a reference prototype had been built and run against the merged hooks (as that file itself says), and before any change to the three shipped files. The receipt gate (386 cases) and the wiring (W02 to W06) were pre-registered only by the one-line predictions G5 and G9 of the first file, with no wanted verdict fixed per case. hooks/README.md should say 314 of the 740 cases had their verdict fixed in advance, not "every test case".
findings.how_it_arises: This is not a gate behaviour. It is the statement the owner reads first in the PR, and the owner decided to merge only after an outside audit. A reader who takes "before any test run" at face value treats the 188-RED prediction and the receipt evidence as blind tests, which the records do not support: the pre-registration itself says they are not blind, and six receipt cases were relabelled after the red run, so every case that names a finding fails on the old gate by construction.

findings.title: The pull request changes the prompt classifier (govclass.py), which it says is left for a second pull request. Owner prompts that quote a harness marker are now classified, so the prompt trigger fires and the Stop gate's prompt-class rule can block where the merged hooks stayed silent. No commit message or PR line says so.
findings.component: hooks/govclass.py (changed in c224c94); pr-36-body.md 'What this is' and 'What changes'; commit c224c94 message
findings.rule_quoted: pr-36-body.md line 9: "The other units (classifier and prompt trigger, ...) go into a second pull request." Commit c224c94: "Not in this commit: the receipt gate, the classifier's word lists, the prompt trigger, ...". hooks/README.md line 74 (still standing): "the blocking classifier is unchanged".

findings.expected: Either 'What changes' names the change, or the PR stops saying the classifier and prompt trigger are untouched here. The change: the classifier now treats a marker as harness text only at the start of the text, and it imports turngate, so the prompt trigger and the Stop gate's prompt-class rule now act on prompts that quote a marker. The behaviour itself looks like what the rule intends (the honest neighbour with governors loaded still passes). The defect is the statement.
findings.how_it_arises: Any owner prompt that quotes notification or command markers now gets the auto-trigger and can be blocked at stop. That happens often when the owner discusses these hooks. The owner was told the classifier was deferred, so a new block would look like a regression in a unit that did not change. The same change has a second effect: govclass now imports turngate, so with turngate.py missing the prompt trigger goes silent. The README's missing-file table does say 'let through, not judged' for prompts.

findings.title: The receipt evidence says the gate was not tuned to the real record. In fact, the earlier build's blocks on the record were seen, and the claim family behind two of them was then switched off. The PR lists NOT_VERIFIED_IS_A_CLAIM = False as a plain default and does not say that this one setting removes two real blocks.
findings.rule_quoted: replay-vs-baseline.md line 31: "The gate was not tuned to the record: no rule, word or case of this fix was written from these three answers." decisions.md: "An inability claim ("couldn't verify" and its variants, contractions included) needs a receipt in the same sentence."
findings.expected: The sentence about tuning claims only what it can support: no rule was written from the three answers that are still blocked, and the family that blocked two other real stops was switched off after those blocks were seen, for a stated reason. The PR's open decision on NOT_VERIFIED_IS_A_CLAIM says what it decides on the real record (2 of 26 stops), as the PR already does for RECEIPT_SCOPE. Whether this default matches the owner's rule ('and its variants') is for the owner to decide.
findings.how_it_arises: The owner reads 'not tuned to the record' as meaning the 3 blocks out of 26 stops are a blind result. The record says the build before the prose scan blocked 5. The shipped default that brings it down to 3 is one the owner was not asked about. The second auditor's reading (True) is the one the replay shows would block more.

notes: Most numeric claims hold: 740/740, 352/352, 420=420, guard PASS, the replay totals, the prose-scan counts, --needs 16, wrapper 11 cases. The defects are in what the PR says about its own method (AC-1, AC-2, AC-4) and in one behaviour change it does not mention (AC-3). MORE: prose_probe.py and prose-scan.md call list 4 'not tuned against', and c52e3ad says 'on the list that was not tuned against, 3 of 40'. But the grammar was changed once after list 4's first run (RLD204), which took it from 4 of 40 to 3 of 40; low overclaim. MORE: red-on-start.txt relabelled six receipt cases that carried a finding's number and passed on the old gate to 'control' or 'new rule', so the PR's '176 fail on the old gate' is true by construction (folded into AC-1). MORE: the hooks/README.md receipt status says 'the three answers were not read for the fix', while replay-vs-baseline.md says the orchestrator read them after the gate was finished. The two agree only if 'for the fix' means 'to build it'; wording. MORE: the hooks/README.md status block dates the receipt rebuild 2026-11-15, but its commits 9708c5d and c52e3ad are dated 2026-11-16 00:19 UTC; cosmetic. MORE: CORE-SPEC.md step 0 names a pre-registration file 'hypothesis-2026-11-14-turn-gates-fix.md' and step 1 a red-run file under results/2026-11-14/. The shipped files are hypothesis-2026-11-15-turn-gates-cases.md and results/2026-11-15/; drift between the spec and what shipped, cosmetic. MORE: selftest-turn-gates.py and selftest-mutations.py (both in hooks/) carry hand-set values (e.g. HOOK_WAIT_SECONDS) that are not in the registry, and changing HOOK_WAIT_SECONDS leaves registry_check at PASS. The fix's own text claims only the gate modules are registered, but the older README line 'Every hand-set value in this directory is now registered' still stands; for fa-surfaces. MORE: DELEGATE_MAY_MERGE = True is listed as an open default, while decisions.md asks that silent cases default to 'fail closed for merges'. Whether the rule is silent here is for the merge auditor and the owner. Each pair of commits (c224c94/4dedf62, 9708c5d/c52e3ad, 10461ae/c3c8615) shares the same second as author and commit time; the per-commit guard claims were checked for c224c94 and 9708c5d and hold. The report is saved at WORK/fa-claims/findings.json, and the reproductions are in WORK/fa-claims/repro_claims.sh.
